모세(Moses)는 기원전 1526년경 이집트에서 태어났습니다. 레위 지: Moses was born in Egypt around 1526 B.C. He came from the tribe of Levi and was raised by Pharaoh's daughter, but at 40 he fled into the wilderness and spent 40 years as a shepherd in Midian, and then received God's call at Mount Horeb. After that he led the people of Israel out of Egypt, received the Law at Mount Sinai, and wrote the Pentateuch (Genesis–Deuteronomy). The Ezra course sees Moses as 'the mediator of the Law' and 'a type of Christ.'
Joshua came from the tribe of Ephraim and was Moses' servant. He was the leader of Israel who led the war to conquer Canaan, and he divided up the land God had promised. As his name means, 'the LORD is salvation,' he is the original of the name of Jesus Christ (Jesus = Joshua).
사무엘서의 저자는 사무엘 선지자로 추정되나, 사무엘의 사후 기록은 나단·: Samuel the prophet is thought to have written the books of Samuel, but the records after Samuel's death are known to have been continued by the prophets Nathan and Gad (1 Chr 29:29). Samuel was the last judge of Israel and the founder of the first school of prophets (the company of prophets at Ramah).
시편은 다윗(73편), 아삽(12편), 고라 자손(11편), 솔로몬(2편: The Psalms are the Bible's 'hymnbook,' written over hundreds of years by many authors: David (73 psalms), Asaph (12), the sons of Korah (11), Solomon (2), Moses (1), Ethan (1), and others. The Ezra course sees the Psalms as the very essence of Hebrew poetry, the book that holds God's heart most deeply.
솔로몬은 다윗의 아들로 이스라엘 통일왕국 제3대 왕(재위 약 B.C. 9: Solomon, the son of David, was the third king of the united kingdom of Israel (reigned c. 970–931 B.C.). The king of wisdom, he wrote Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, and Song of Songs, and built the temple in Jerusalem (the First Temple). The Ezra course sees Solomon as 'a type of Christ's wisdom and glory.'
이사야(Isaiah, '여호와는 구원이시다')는 B.C. 8세기 남유다의: Isaiah ('the LORD is salvation') was a major prophet of the southern kingdom of Judah in the 8th century B.C., a contemporary of Amos and Hosea. He is thought to have come from the royal family, and he prophesied for about 40 years in the days of Kings Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah. Because its messianic prophecies (Isa 7:14; chapter 53) are so exact, the book of Isaiah is called 'the gospel of the Old Testament.'
예레미야(Jeremiah)는 B.C. 626년 소명을 받은 '눈물의 선지: Jeremiah, 'the weeping prophet,' was called in 626 B.C. and served for about 40 years, from just before the fall of Judah to the early Babylonian Exile. He came from a priestly family of Anathoth and called for repentance even under severe persecution. Lamentations is also his work, written in grief over the fall of Jerusalem.
에스겔(Ezekiel)은 바벨론 포로기(B.C. 597~571)에 활동한: Ezekiel was a prophet from a priestly family who served during the Babylonian Exile (597–571 B.C.). He received his call by the river Chebar in a vision of the throne of God's glory. His apocalyptic prophecies, such as the dry bones coming to life (Ezek 37) and the vision of the new temple (Ezek 40–48), are what mark the book.
다니엘(Daniel)은 유다 왕족 출신으로 B.C. 605년 느부갓네살의: Daniel was a young man of Judah's royal family who was taken to Babylon in 605 B.C., during Nebuchadnezzar's first invasion. He purposed in his heart to refuse the king's food and feared God alone, and with the gift of interpreting dreams and his apocalyptic visions he bore witness to God's sovereignty in the courts of Babylon and Persia.
에스라(Ezra)는 대제사장 아론의 16대손으로 바벨론에서 귀환한 서기관: Ezra was a priest and scribe, a 16th-generation descendant of the high priest Aaron, who returned from Babylon. A scholar skilled in the Law, he taught God's statutes and ordinances to the people of Israel. He wrote Ezra–Nehemiah (originally one book), and tradition also credits him with Chronicles.
느헤미야(Nehemiah)는 페르시아 아닥사스다 1세 왕의 술 관원으로,: Nehemiah was cupbearer to King Artaxerxes I of Persia, and in 445 B.C. he returned to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem. He finished the walls in 52 days and governed Judah for 12 years. Together with Ezra he led a reform of faith and a revival of the Law.
마태(Matthew, 레위)는 가버나움의 세리(세금 징수원)였으나 예수님: Matthew (Levi) was a tax collector in Capernaum, but he was called by Jesus and became a disciple. He wrote the Gospel of Matthew for Jewish Christians, to prove that Jesus is the Messiah King of the Old Testament. Its five great discourses (such as the Sermon on the Mount) are its mark.
마가(Mark, 요한 마가)는 바나바의 사촌으로 바울의 1차 전도여행에: Mark (John Mark) was Barnabas's cousin; he joined Paul's first missionary journey but left partway. He is known as Peter's interpreter, and the Gospel of Mark was written from Peter's memories. Written for Roman readers, it presents Jesus as 'the Servant of power,' and its vivid, on-the-scene detail is its mark.
Luke was a Greek physician (Col 4:14) and Paul's co-worker. Of the 27 New Testament books he wrote two: the Gospel of Luke, the longest, and Acts. Along with a historian's accuracy, he stresses Jesus' love for the outcast (women, tax collectors, sinners). His central theme is 'Christ who came as the Son of Man.'
요한(John)은 세베대의 아들로 예수님의 '사랑하시는 제자'입니다. 열: John, son of Zebedee, was Jesus' 'beloved disciple.' He lived the longest of the twelve apostles and served mainly in Ephesus. He wrote the Gospel of John, 1, 2, and 3 John, and Revelation. The Ezra course stresses the Gospel of John as 'the gospel of the incarnation, where the Word became flesh.'
바울(Paul, 히브리어 사울)은 베냐민 지파 출신 로마 시민권자로 가말: Paul (Saul in Hebrew) was a Roman citizen from the tribe of Benjamin and a teacher of the Law trained under Gamaliel. On the road to Damascus he met the risen Christ and became the apostle to the Gentiles. He wrote 13 letters, including Romans, Galatians, 1 and 2 Corinthians, and Ephesians.
베드로(Peter)는 어부 출신으로 예수님으로부터 '반석'(케파)이라는: Peter, a fisherman, was the leading disciple, who received from Jesus the name 'rock' (Cephas). After the Holy Spirit came at Pentecost he became the center of the mission to the Jews, and he wrote 1 and 2 Peter, urging the scattered believers of Asia Minor to hope and holy living in the midst of persecution.
야고보(James)는 예수님의 형제(갈 1:19)로, 초대 예루살렘 교회: James was the brother of Jesus (Gal 1:19) and a leader of the early church in Jerusalem. The letter of James is thought to be the earliest of the New Testament letters (c. A.D. 45–49). It stresses a faith that is lived out: 'by works was faith made perfect.'
히브리서의 저자는 바울·아볼로·바나바·브리스길라 등 다양한 설이 있으나: There are many views on who wrote Hebrews (Paul, Apollos, Barnabas, Priscilla, and others), but it has not been settled. It is a theological masterpiece that carefully shows how the Old Testament sacrifices, the tabernacle, and the Levitical priesthood are fulfilled in Christ.
유다(Jude)는 예수님의 형제(마 13:55)입니다. 당시 교회를 위협: Jude was the brother of Jesus (Matt 13:55). He warns against the false teachers (the licentious) who threatened the church at that time, and urges, 'remember ye the words which were spoken before of the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ.'
모세오경 기록 시기는 이스라엘이 출애굽(B.C. 1446년경)하여 가나안: The Pentateuch was written around the time Israel came out of Egypt (c. 1446 B.C.) and was finishing the conquest of Canaan. This was the golden age of ancient Egypt's New Kingdom (18th–19th Dynasties), and the reign of Thutmose III, before Ramesses II, draws attention as the historical background of the Exodus. The Ezra course sees this period as 'the birth of the nation of Israel and the age when the constitution of God's kingdom (the Law) was given.'
이 시기는 이스라엘 통일왕국(사울·다윗·솔로몬)과 분열왕국 초기에 해당합: This period covers the united kingdom of Israel (Saul, David, Solomon) and the early divided kingdom (c. 1050–900 B.C.). In the Near East, surrounding nations such as Aram-Damascus, Moab, and the Philistines were strong. The Ezra course sees this period as the age when 'the covenant with David, the completion of Solomon's temple, and then the tragedy of division caused by idolatry' began.
이 시기는 북이스라엘이 앗수르에 멸망(B.C. 722)하고 남유다가 위기: This was a turbulent age: the northern kingdom of Israel fell to Assyria (722 B.C.) and the southern kingdom of Judah faced crisis. While the Assyrian Empire at its height (Shalmaneser V, Sennacherib) stood face to face with Egypt's 25th Dynasty (Cush/Ethiopia), the prophets Isaiah, Micah, Habakkuk, and Zephaniah were at work.
바벨론 포로기(B.C. 605~538년)로, 느부갓네살의 3차례 예루살렘: This is the Babylonian Exile (605–538 B.C.): Nebuchadnezzar's three attacks on Jerusalem, the destruction of the temple (586 B.C.), and 70 years of captivity in Babylon. Ezekiel and Daniel were at work in this period, and 'the Exile' was both the greatest crisis of Israel's faith and a time of growing up. The Ezra course sees this period as 'the age when God's judgment and the promise of restoration came at the same time.'
바벨론 포로귀환 시대(B.C. 538~400년경)로, 페르시아 고레스 왕: This is the age of the Return from Exile (c. 538–400 B.C.). By the decree of King Cyrus of Persia, Israel returned in three waves (Zerubbabel, Ezra, Nehemiah). It was the time when the Second Temple was rebuilt and the Law restored, the last age of the Old Testament.
신약 기록 시기(A.D. 45~100년경)입니다. 로마 황제 클라우디우스: This is the age when the New Testament was written (c. A.D. 45–100). Under the Roman emperors Claudius, Nero, and Domitian the early church was persecuted, yet the gospel spread across the world. All 27 books of the New Testament were written in this period, around the destruction of the Jerusalem temple (A.D. 70).
